note: Derived from RequirementRegister.for_phase("24"): 4 MANDATORY requirements owned by lifecycle.evolution. All four are pre-existing register entries (MS §Child Products / VDC §Child evolution), not added this phase. This phase implements the Product Evolution SDK for AI-Native Self-Evolving child products that already exist -- it does not build initial child-product generation (tracked separately and permanently as DEF-009, docs/build/OPEN_BLOCKERS.md), which is out of this phase's canonical scope.

claims.implementation: child_product_identity.ChildProductMode declares exactly the three MS-named modes (STANDARD, AI_ASSISTED, AI_NATIVE_SELF_EVOLVING) and no fourth can be constructed. ChildProductIdentity.uses_evolution_sdk is the single place SDK eligibility is decided (AI_NATIVE_SELF_EVOLVING only); declare_child_product_campaign and promote_child_product both consult it and refuse before constructing anything for an ineligible mode.
claims.evidence: integ: test_child_product_identity.py::TestChildProductMode (exactly three modes, a fourth refused) and ::TestChildProductIdentity::test_only_ai_native_self_evolving_uses_the_sdk; test_child_product_campaign.py::TestModeEligibilityRefusesBeforeConstruction and test_child_product_promotion.py::TestPromoteChildProductFullFlow::test_non_sdk_eligible_mode_is_refused compose the eligibility check with real campaign declaration and real promotion end to end.
claims.note: The single register evidence key (integ) is supplied.

claims.implementation: The full C-36 lifecycle is real and composed: child_product_campaign.declare_child_product_campaign/begin_child_product_campaign (declaration), child_product_workspace.allocate_child_product_workspace (isolated working copy, reusing Phase 12's WorkspaceAuthority), child_product_promotion.promote_child_product (candidate -> accepted -> scoped HUMAN_GATE_3 grant -> promoted, the only production path that advances a lineage with new content), child_product_rollback.rollback_child_product (restore to an already-approved version, a separate authority per ADR-0009). No step is a stub: every one raises real, typed refusals before any mutation.
claims.evidence: integ: test_child_product_promotion.py (26 tests: scoped-grant lookup against a real GovernanceState/HUMAN_GATE_RECORDS.md copy, full-flow ordering) and test_child_product_rollback.py (12 tests: real lineage restore, receipt, cross-product isolation). run: test_child_product_journey.py::TestComposedChildProductEvolutionJourney::test_the_full_two_cycle_journey -- real filesystem workspace, real SQLite via the real Alembic chain, real C-14/C-15 evidence registration, two full evolution cycles (declare, allocate, candidate, refuse-then-grant-then-promote, evolve again, rollback), full history/evidence verified intact at the end.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys (integ, run) are supplied. A real defect was found running the journey test (child_product_campaign._child_campaign_id collided across two evolution requests for the same product, since it depended on product identity alone) and repaired before this candidate froze -- fixed to bind campaign_id to (product_ref, objective) together, content-addressed; the corrected property is what this claim's evidence proves, not the earlier, defective one.

claims.implementation: declare_child_product_campaign/begin_child_product_campaign compose evolution_campaign_state_machine.build() -- the real, unmodified Phase 23 EvolutionCampaign machine (STATE_MACHINES.md §10) and CampaignDeclaration/CampaignBudgets (the six MS-named budgets) directly, never a second campaign model. MS states plainly that Product Evolution SDK cycles "use the same bounded campaign model, budgets and terminal states as ARKALI Self-Evolution"; no second StateMachineDefinition is minted and lifecycle.evolution gains no second state_machine_authorities entry.
claims.evidence: prop: test_child_product_campaign.py::TestBeginsTheRealUnmodifiedEvolutionCampaignMachine::test_the_instance_is_a_real_evolution_campaign_machine_instance asserts instance.machine.definition IS ecsm.DEFINITION (identity, not equality) for any declared child campaign; test_child_product_adversarial.py::TestCampaignRestartManipulation::test_a_terminal_child_campaign_cannot_be_restarted proves TerminalStateEscape is raised for any transition attempted from any of the four terminal states, and ::test_no_new_state_machine_authority_was_minted_for_child_products restates the identity proof; test_child_product_adversarial.py::TestNoShadowAuthority::test_no_duplicate_state_machine_or_canonical_authority_exists re-runs the live duplicate_state_machine_authority/duplicate_canonical_authority/duplicate_lifecycle_authority/shadow_registry architecture gates as an explicit adversarial assertion.
claims.note: The single register evidence key (prop) is supplied, proven as a structural/behavioural property over the real machine rather than one example instance.

claims.implementation: child_product_promotion.py and child_product_rollback.py import neither lifecycle.release nor lifecycle.recovery -- neither can reach ARKALI's own StableRevisionPointer or RecoverySupervisor at all, structurally, not by convention. A child product's own version lineage (child_product_version.py) is a distinct, per-product record from ARKALI's single Stable Core pointer, mirroring its discipline without sharing its instance. child_product_workspace.py never resolves a path outside its caller-supplied stable_snapshot parameter (no repository-root constant, no __file__-relative upward path, no import of engineering.candidate beyond the Protocol-only reach).
claims.evidence: run: test_child_product_journey.py's composed two-cycle journey proves promotion and rollback both complete for real against only the child's own lineage, never touching any ARKALI-core object (none is even constructed in the fixture set). arch: test_child_product_adversarial.py::TestNoDirectStableOrLiveMutationAnywhereInTheChildProductSdk (AST: no import of lifecycle.release/lifecycle.recovery anywhere in child_product_*.py, no reference to StableRevisionPointer's own promote/rollback_to method names outside the two sanctioned, differently-named child-product methods) and test_child_product_workspace.py::TestNeverReachesArkaliOwnSource (AST: no repository-root reference).
claims.note: Both register evidence keys (run, arch) are supplied. A real naming collision (child_product_version.py's own rollback method originally shared StableRevisionPointer.rollback_to's exact name) was found by running Phase 23's own structural test and repaired by renaming the child-product method (restore_to) rather than loosening that security-critical test -- the more conservative fix, since it required zero changes to Phase 23's own accepted control.
